proposal.hypothesis: LiBr is a wide-gap, Li-rich halide whose Li+ and Br- ions are hard to oxidize or reduce against Li6PS5Cl. Its halide chemistry is close to the low-penalty LiF and LiCaAlF6 results, and the Cl-/Br- exchange with the Cl-containing sulfide should be nearly thermoneutral. The main risk is bromide oxidation near 4.0 V, so it is a test of whether a heavier halide can match the fluorides.
